contextRef="c-1" name="us-gaap:OrganizationConsolidationAndPresentationOfFinancialStatementsDisclosureTextBlock" id="f-44" continuedAt="f-44-1" escape="true"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-36pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">1.&#160;Organization</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Blackstone Multi-Strategy Hedge Fund L.P. (&#8220;BXHF&#8221;) is a Delaware limited partnership formed on October 28, 2025 and a private fund exempt from registration under Section 3(c)(7) of the Investment Company Act of 1940, as amended (the &#8220;1940 Act&#8221;). BXHF is structured as a perpetual-life strategy, with monthly, fully funded subscriptions and periodic redemptions.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">BXHF expects to conduct a continuous private offering of its limited partnership units (&#8220;Units&#8221;) in reliance on exemptions from the registration requirements of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the &#8220;1933 Act&#8221;), to investors that are both (a) accredited investors (as defined in Regulation D under the Securities Act) and (b) qualified purchasers (as defined in the 1940 Act and rules thereunder).</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">BXHF&#8217;s investment objective is to generate attractive long-term risk-adjusted returns across market cycles. BXHF will seek to meet its investment objective by investing dynamically in liquid and semi-liquid opportunities across four strategies: credit, equities, special situations and trading, each of which may have several underlying sub-strategies.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">As of March&#160;31, 2026, BXHF had not commenced investment operations. Certain subsidiaries were formed during the quarter for the purpose of supporting future investment activities. BXHF&#8217;s fiscal year ends on December 31 of each year.</span></div></ix:nonNumeric><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"><ix:continuation id="f-44-1">Blackstone Alternative Asset Management Associates LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, is BXHF&#8217;s general partner (the &#8220;General Partner&#8221;). Overall responsibility for oversight of BXHF rests with the General Partner, subject to certain oversight rights held by BXHF&#8217;s board of directors (the &#8220;Board of Directors&#8221;). The General Partner will delegate BXHF&#8217;s portfolio management function to Blackstone Alternative Asset Management L.P., a Delaware limited partnership (the &#8220;Investment Manager&#8221;). The Investment Manager will have discretion to make investments on behalf of BXHF. The Investment Manager expects to enter into a sub-investment management agreement (as may be amended, supplemented, restated or otherwise modified from time to time, the &#8220;Sub-Investment Management Agreement&#8221;) with Blackstone Alternative Solutions L.L.C. (the &#8220;Affiliated Sub-Investment Manager&#8221; and together with the Investment Manager, the &#8220;BXHF Managers&#8221;) pursuant to which the Investment Manager expects to delegate the portfolio management function for a portion of BXHF&#8217;s investments to the Affiliated Sub-Investment Manager. The BXHF Managers will be responsible for initiating, structuring, and negotiating BXHF&#8217;s investments. In addition, the BXHF Managers will actively manage and monitor each investment, as applicable, to seek to maximize value. Each of the BXHF Managers is registered with the United States Securities and Exchange Commission (&#8220;SEC&#8221;) as an investment adviser under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940, as amended (the &#8220;Advisers Act&#8221;). The General Partner, the Investment Manager or the Affiliated Sub-Investment Manager will provide administration services to BXHF and are individually and collectively referred to as the &#8220;Sponsor.&#8221; Each of the General Partner, Investment Manager and the Affiliated Sub-Investment Manager are affiliates of Blackstone Inc. (&#8220;Blackstone&#8221;).</ix:continuation> </span></div><div id="ie8493a2e77294448bf738d7b5cb3d914_406"></div><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c-1" name="us-gaap:SignificantAccountingPoliciesTextBlock" id="f-45" continuedAt="f-45-1" escape="true"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-36pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">2.&#160;Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</span></div><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c-1" name="us-gaap:BasisOfAccountingPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="f-46" escape="true"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Basis of Presentation</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The accompanying unaudited consolidated financial statement of BXHF has been prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (&#8220;GAAP&#8221;). BXHF is considered an investment company under GAAP and follows the accounting and reporting guidance applicable to investment companies in the Financial Accounting Standards Board Accounting Standards Codification Topic 946,&#160;</span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Financial Services&#8212;Investment Companies </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">("ASC 946"). The consolidated financial statement, including the notes, is unaudited. Management believes it has made all necessary adjustments (consisting of only normal recurring items), if applicable, so that the consolidated financial statement is presented fairly. The operating results presented for interim periods are not necessarily indicative of the results that may be expected for any other interim period or for the entire year.</span></div></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c-1" name="us-gaap:UseOfEstimates" id="f-47" escape="true"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Use of Estimates</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The preparation of the consolidated financial statement in conformity with GAAP requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities and disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities at the date of the consolidated financial statement. Management believes that estimates made in preparing its consolidated financial statement are reasonable. Actual results may ultimately differ materially from those estimates.</span></div></ix:nonNumeric></ix:nonNumeric><div style="height:36pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div id="f-45-1"><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c-1" name="us-gaap:ConsolidationPolicyTextBlock" id="f-48" escape="true"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Principles of Consolidation</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">In accordance with ASC 946, BXHF generally does not consolidate its investments unless it has a controlling financial interest in an investment company or in an operating company whose business consists of providing services to BXHF. When such a controlling financial interest exists, the results of the related reporting entities are consolidated, and all intercompany balances and transactions are eliminated in consolidation.</span></div></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c-1" name="us-gaap:CashAndCashEquivalentsPolicyTextBlock" id="f-49" continuedAt="f-49-1" escape="true"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Cash and Cash Equivalents</span></div></ix:nonNumeric><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"><ix:continuation id="f-49-1">Cash and Cash Equivalents represents cash on hand, cash held in banks, money market funds and liquid investments with original maturities of three months or less.</ix:continuation> </span></div><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c-1" name="bxhf:OfferingAndOrganizationalCostsPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="f-50" continuedAt="f-50-1" escape="true"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Organizational and Offering Expenses</span></div></ix:nonNumeric><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"><ix:continuation id="f-50-1">Organizational and offering costs will only be borne by BXHF when BXHF first accepts third-party investors and commences investment operations, at which time, costs associated with the organization of BXHF will be expensed as incurred. Costs associated with the offering of Units of BXHF will be capitalized as a deferred expense and included as an asset on the Statement of Assets and Liabilities and amortized over a twelve-month period from incurrence. As of March 31, 2026, BXHF had not accepted any third-party investors and investment operations have not yet commenced, therefore organizational and offering expenses are not recorded in the accompanying Statement of Assets and Liabilities.</ix:continuation> For additional information relating to organizational and offering expenses, please see Note 4. &#8220;Commitments and Contingencies.&#8221; </span></div><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c-1" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxPolicyTextBlock" id="f-51" escape="true"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Income Taxes</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">BXHF is treated as a partnership for income tax purposes and is not subject to income taxes. Certain intermediate entities that may be formed for use in carrying out the activities of BXHF following the commencement of operations may be subject to income taxes.</span></div></ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation><div id="ie8493a2e77294448bf738d7b5cb3d914_423"></div><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c-1" name="us-gaap:RelatedPartyTransactionsDisclosureTextBlock" id="f-52" continuedAt="f-52-1" escape="true"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-36pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">3.&#160;Related Party Transactions</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Partnership Agreement</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">BXHF has entered into a limited partnership agreement (the &#8220;BXHF Partnership Agreement&#8221;) with the General Partner. Overall responsibility for BXHF&#8217;s oversight rests with the General Partner, subject to certain oversight rights held by BXHF&#8217;s Board of Directors. The General Partner will delegate BXHF&#8217;s portfolio management function to the Investment Manager. </span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Performance Participation Allocation</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The General Partner will be allocated a performance participation (the &#8220;Performance Participation Allocation&#8221;) by BXHF directly or indirectly through an intermediate entity equal to <ix:nonFraction unitRef="number" contextRef="c-5" decimals="3" name="us-gaap:ManagementAndServiceFeesIncentiveRate" scale="-2" id="f-53">12.5</ix:nonFraction>% of BXHF&#8217;s total return subject to a <ix:nonFraction unitRef="number" contextRef="c-6" decimals="3" name="us-gaap:ManagementAndServiceFeesIncentiveRate" scale="-2" id="f-54">5</ix:nonFraction>% annual hurdle amount and a high water mark with <ix:nonFraction unitRef="number" contextRef="c-7" decimals="3" name="us-gaap:ManagementAndServiceFeesIncentiveRate" scale="-2" id="f-55">100</ix:nonFraction>%&#160;catch-up.&#160;Such allocation will be measured on a calendar year basis, be paid quarterly and accrued monthly (subject to&#160;pro-rating&#160;for partial periods). For the first calendar year of BXHF&#8217;s operations, the allocation will be paid at the end of such first calendar year and thereafter the allocation will be paid quarterly. Each class or series of the Fund, any Feeder Vehicle (as defined below) and/or any Parallel Fund (as applicable, as defined below) will bear (without duplication) the Performance Participation Allocation applicable to such class or series based on its corresponding interest in the Aggregator (as defined below). The General Partner may elect to receive the Performance Participation Allocation in cash, units of BXHF or any Parallel Fund and/or shares, units or interests (as applicable) of intermediate entities. If the Performance Participation Allocation is paid in Units, such Units may be redeemed at the General Partner&#8217;s request and will be subject to certain volume limitations.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Investment Management Agreement</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">BXHF intends to enter into an investment management agreement with the Investment Manager (as may be amended, supplemented, restated or otherwise modified from time to time, the &#8220;Investment Management Agreement&#8221;). As part of carrying out its investment management services, the Investment Manager may enter into sub-advisory, or other similar arrangements, with other advisory subsidiaries of Blackstone. These sub-advisory relationships do not affect the terms of the Investment Management Agreement.</span></div></ix:nonNumeric><div style="height:36pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div Fee</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">In consideration for its Each class or series of the Fund, any Feeder Vehicle and/or any Parallel Fund (as applicable) will bear (without duplication) the Management Fee applicable to such class or series based on its corresponding interest in the Aggregator. The Management Fee will be calculated by the Sponsor.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The Investment Manager may elect to receive the Management Fee in cash, Units of the Fund, units of any Parallel Fund and/or shares, units or interests (as applicable) of intermediate entities. Additionally, the Investment Manager may separately elect for the Management Fee to be paid (in whole or in part) to an affiliate of the Investment Manager in satisfaction of Management Fee amounts owed to the Investment Manager in connection with services provided by such affiliate to BXHF and/or any intermediate entity. From time to time, the Sponsor, out of its own resources and without additional cost to BXHF or its investors, may offer other discounts, waivers or other incentives to investors.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Administration Fee</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The Investment Manager will provide administration services to BXHF, consistent with the BXHF Partnership Agreement and Investment Management Agreement. Each of the Fund, any Feeder Vehicle and/or any Parallel Fund (as applicable) will bear (without duplication) its proportional share of the Administration Fee based on its proportional interest in the Aggregator.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The Administration Fee will include BXHF&#8217;s proportional share of any administrative services provided to any consolidated underlying investment vehicles but will be separate from and additional to the Management Fee and other fund expenses, including administrative expenses incurred in connection with certain investments,&#160;non-consolidated&#160;portfolio entities and the middle- and back-office services provided by a certain third-party provider.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The Investment Manager may engage a third-party administrator (the &#8220;Administrator&#8221;) on behalf of BXHF to provide certain administration services. The fees, costs and expenses for such administrative services performed by the Administrator will be payable by the Investment Manager out of its Administration Fee.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Dealer Manager Agreement</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">BXHF intends to enter into a Dealer Manager Agreement (as may be amended, supplemented, restated or otherwise modified from time to time, the &#8220;Dealer Manager Agreement&#8221;) with Blackstone Securities Partners L.P. (the &#8220;Dealer Manager&#8221;), a broker-dealer registered with the SEC under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the "Exchange Act&#8221;) and a member of the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority. The Dealer Manager also coordinates BXHF&#8217;s marketing and distribution efforts with participating brokers and their registered representatives with respect to communications related to the terms As of March 31, 2026, BXHF was not subject to any material litigation nor was BXHF aware of any material litigation threatened against it. </span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Indemnifications</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">In the normal course of business, BXHF enters into contracts that contain a variety of indemnification arrangements. BXHF&#8217;s exposure under these arrangements, if any, cannot be quantified. However, BXHF has not had any claims or losses pursuant to these indemnification arrangements and expects the potential for a material loss to be remote as of March&#160;31, 2026.</span></div></ix:continuation><div id="ie8493a2e77294448bf738d7b5cb3d914_465"></div><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c-1" name="us-gaap:StockholdersEquityNoteDisclosureTextBlock" id="f-63" escape="true"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-36pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">5.&#160;Net Assets</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">BXHF intends to offer <ix:nonFraction unitRef="class" contextRef="c-3" decimals="INF" name="bxhf:NumberOfClassesOfLimitedPartnershipUnits" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="0" id="f-64">three</ix:nonFraction> classes, or series of classes of limited partnership Units: Class&#160;I, Class&#160;S and Class&#160;D Units and may offer additional classes, or series of classes of Units in the future. BXHF, at the discretion of the General Partner, expects to have the authority to issue an unlimited number of Units of each class, or series of a class. The purchase price per Unit of each class, or series of a class,&#160;is equal to the NAV per Unit for such class, or series of a class,&#160;as of the last calendar day of the immediately preceding month. Until BXHF has determined its first NAV, the subscription price for Units will be $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="usdPerShare" contextRef="c-3" decimals="2" name="us-gaap:NetAssetValuePerShare" scale="0" id="f-65">25.00</ix:nonFraction> per Unit plus applicable subscription fees.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">NAV for each Unit class,&#160;or series of a class, will first be determined as of the end of the first full month after BXHF has accepted third-party investors and commenced investment operations. Thereafter, the NAV for each class,&#160;or series of a class, of Units will be calculated monthly by the Sponsor. The NAV will be based on the&#160;month-end&#160;values of investments, the addition of the value of any other assets such as cash, and the deduction of any liabilities, including the accrual and allocation of the Management Fee, Administration Fee and the Performance Participation Allocation and the deduction of expenses attributable to certain classes or series of classes, of Units, such as applicable Servicing Fees.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Certain financial intermediaries through which a unitholder is placed in BXHF may charge the unitholder upfront selling commissions, placement fees, subscription fees or similar fees (&#8220;Subscription Fees&#8221;) of up to (a)&#160;<ix:nonFraction unitRef="number" contextRef="c-13" decimals="3" name="bxhf:InvestmentCompanyIncentiveFees" scale="-2" id="f-66">3.5</ix:nonFraction>% of NAV on Class&#160;S Units and (b) <ix:nonFraction unitRef="number" contextRef="c-14" decimals="3" name="bxhf:InvestmentCompanyIncentiveFees" scale="-2" id="f-67">1.5</ix:nonFraction>% of NAV on Class&#160;D Units sold in the offering. These Subscription Fees are paid by the unitholder outside of its investment in BXHF and not reflected in BXHF&#8217;s net asset value.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">On December&#160;17, 2025, the General Partner made an initial capital contribution of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="usd" contextRef="c-15" decimals="-3" name="us-gaap:InvestmentCompanyCommittedCapital" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" scale="0" id="f-68">100,000</ix:nonFraction> in exchange for limited partner interests in BXHF. As of March&#160;31, 2026, the General Partner was BXHF&#8217;s only interest holder.</span></div></ix:nonNumeric><div id="ie8493a2e77294448bf738d7b5cb3d914_483"></div><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c-1" name="us-gaap:DebtDisclosureTextBlock" id="f-69" continuedAt="f-69-1" escape="true"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-36pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">6.&#160;Warehousing Agreement</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">On December&#160;18, 2025, Finco, the Investment Manager on behalf of BXHF, and not for its own account, and BXHF entered into the Warehousing Agreement. Under the Warehousing Agreement, in connection with the launch of BXHF, Finco has agreed to acquire, directly or through its affiliates, certain investments that have been approved by BXHF&#8217;s investment committee (or its delegate) up to an aggregate invested equity amount of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="usd" contextRef="c-16" decimals="-5" name="us-gaap:WarehouseAgreementBorrowings" scale="6" id="f-70">500</ix:nonFraction> million (or such higher amount as is agreed between the parties), subject in each case, to Finco&#8217;s approval at the time of acquisition (each, an &#8220;Approved Warehoused Investment&#8221;). Finco has agreed to subsequently transfer each Approved Warehoused Investment to BXHF, and BXHF has agreed to acquire such investments from Finco, on the terms described in the Warehousing Agreement following the point or points in time at which BXHF has sufficient capital to acquire such investments, as determined by the Investment Manager in its sole discretion (each such date, a &#8220;Warehouse Closing Date&#8221;).</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">On each Warehouse Closing Date, BXHF will acquire from Finco each funded Approved Warehoused Investment selected by the Investment Manager for such Warehouse Closing Date at a price equal to the cost of such Approved Warehoused Investment paid by Finco plus an amount equal to an annualized rate of <ix:nonFraction unitRef="number" contextRef="c-17" decimals="3" name="bxhf:WarehouseAgreementBorrowingsInvestmentAcquisitionRate" scale="-2" id="f-71">5</ix:nonFraction>% measured over the period from the date the Approved Warehoused Investment was acquired by Finco to the applicable Warehouse Closing Date. The Investment Manager will determine in its sole discretion which and what portions of Approved Warehoused Investments that BXHF will acquire on each Warehouse Closing Date. Finco will continue to provide committed funding for Approved Warehoused Investments until the applicable Warehouse Closing Date, unless extended by the mutual agreement of the parties. BXHF will bear its proportionate (a)&#160;fees, costs and expenses in connection with the Warehousing Agreement, including fees, costs and expenses, if any, incurred in developing, negotiating and structuring any Approved Warehoused </span></div></ix:nonNumeric><div style="height:36pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="text-align:right"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">10</span></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"/><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div style="text-align:center"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Blackstone Multi-Strategy Hedge Fund L.P.</span></div><div style="text-align:center"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statement (Unaudited)</span></div><div style="text-align:center"><table style="border-collapse:collapse;display:inline-table;margin-bottom:5pt;vertical-align:text-bottom;width:100.000%"><tr><td style="width:1.0%"/><td style="width:32.233%"/><td style="width:0.1%"/><td style="width:1.0%"/><td style="width:32.233%"/><td style="width:0.1%"/><td style="width:1.0%"/><td style="width:32.234%"/><td style="width:0.1%"/></tr><tr><td colspan="9" style="border-bottom:1pt solid #000;padding:2px 1pt;text-align:left;vertical-align:top"><div style="text-align:center"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">(Dollars in Thousands, Except Unit Data)</span></div></td></tr></table></div></div><ix:continuation id="f-69-1"><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Investment that is transferred to BXHF and (b)&#160;broken deal expenses. style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We were organized on October 28, 2025 as a limited partnership under the laws of the State of Delaware. We are a private fund exempt from registration under Section 3(c)(7) of the Investment Company Act of 1940, as amended.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#160;Our investment objective is to generate attractive long-term risk-adjusted returns across market cycles. The Fund aims to balance growth and preservation of capital, and seeks to produce an attractive return with low volatility, low drawdowns and low sensitivity to traditional assets such as stocks and bonds. We will seek to meet our investment objective by investing dynamically in liquid and semi-liquid opportunities across four strategies: Credit, Equities, Special Situations and Trading (collectively, the &#8220;Investment Strategies&#8221;), each of which is expected to have several underlying&#160;sub-strategies.&#160;The Fund is expected to employ Blackstone's unconstrained approach to multi-asset investing, which deploys capital across asset classes in both public and private markets.&#160;</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><span intermediaries supported by detailed and itemized invoices, costs in connection with preparing sales materials, design and website expenses, fees and expenses of each entity (including, as applicable, transfer agent, administrator and depository fees, fees to attend retail seminars sponsored by participating broker-dealers and reimbursements for customary travel, lodging, entertainment and meals, and including all similar organizational and offering expenses of Feeder Vehicles, Parallel Funds and/or Intermediate Entities primarily organized to invest in BXHF to the extent not paid by such Feeder Vehicles, Parallel Funds and/or Intermediate Entities or their investors, but excluding subscription fees and servicing fees)) (collectively, &#8220;Organizational and Offering Expenses&#8221;) through the first anniversary of the date on which BXHF first accepts third-party investors and commences investment operations (the &#8220;Initial Closing Date&#8221;) (such first anniversary, the &#8220;Effective Date&#8221;). On the Initial Closing Date, BXHF will be obligated to reimburse the Investment Manager for all such advanced Organizational and Offering Expenses ratably over the 60 months following the Effective Date or, alternatively, in one or more installments on such earlier date(s) and in such amount(s) as determined by the Investment Manager. In either case, BXHF will recognize a reduction to BXHF&#8217;s Transactional NAV for purposes of subscriptions or redemptions (but not for financial reporting purposes) ratably over the 60 months following the Effective Date. Under accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (&#8220;GAAP&#8221;), costs associated with the organization of BXHF will be expensed upon the Initial Closing Date. Under GAAP, costs associated with the offering of BXHF will be capitalized as deferred expenses and amortized over a&#160;12-month&#160;period from the Initial Closing Date. The Investment Manager will determine what Organizational and Offering Expenses are attributable to BXHF, in its sole discretion. After the Effective Date, BXHF will reimburse the Investment Manager for any Organizational and Offering Expenses that it has incurred on each entity&#8217;s behalf as and when incurred.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Except as specifically provided below, all investment professionals and staff of the Investment Manager, when and to the extent engaged in providing investment management services to BXHF, and the base compensation, bonus and benefits, and the routine overhead expenses, of such personnel allocable to such services, will be provided and paid for by the Investment Manager.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">BXHF will bear all expenses of its operations, including, but not limited to, investment management fees paid to the Investment Manager pursuant to BXHF&#8217;s investment management agreement and&#160;all other expenses of BXHF&#8217;s operations, administrations and transactions. BXHF does not pay fund-level expenses that would be duplicative of services already covered through the administration fee.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Financial Condition, Liquidity and Capital Resources</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">As of May&#160;14, 2026, we have not yet commenced investment operations and do not expect to do so until the Initial Closing Date. On December&#160;17, 2025, the General Partner made an initial capital contribution of $100,000 in exchange for limited partner interests in the Fund. As of March&#160;31, 2026, the General Partner was our only interest holder.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We expect to generate cash primarily from (i)&#160;the net proceeds of our continuous private offering, (ii)&#160;cash flows from our operations and (iii)&#160;any financing arrangements we may enter into in the future.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Our primary use of cash will be for (i)&#160;making Investments, (ii)&#160;the cost of operations (including the management fee of the Investment Manager and performance participation allocation to the General Partner (each as further described in Item 1. Financial Statement)), (iii) debt service of any borrowings, (iv)&#160;periodic redemptions, and (v)&#160;cash distributions, if any, to the holders of our Units.</span></div><div style="height:36pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="text-align:right"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">13</span></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"/><div style="min-height:72pt;width:100%"><div><span><br/></span></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Critical Accounting Estimates</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The preparation of the consolidated financial statement requires us to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets, liabilities, revenues and expenses. Changes in the economic environment, financial markets, and any other parameters used in determining such estimates could cause actual results to differ. For a further discussion about our significant accounting policies, see Note&#160;2. &#8220;Summary of Significant Accounting Policies&#8221; in the &#8220;Notes to Consolidated Financial Statement&#8221; in &#8220;Item&#160;1. Financial Statement&#8221; in this Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Recent Accounting Developments</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">For information regarding recent accounting developments and their impact on BXHF, if any, see Note&#160;2. &#8220;Summary of Significant Accounting Policies&#8221; in the &#8220;Notes to Consolidated Financial Statement&#8221; in &#8220;Item&#160;1. Financial Statement&#8221; in this Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q.</span></div><div id="ie8493a2e77294448bf738d7b5cb3d914_557"></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Item 3.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We will be subject to market risk, which is the risk of potential adverse changes to the value of financial instruments held by us because of changes in market conditions such as interest and currency rate movements and volatility in security prices. We may be exposed to market risk both directly from financial instruments held by us as well as indirectly from the financial instruments held by Underlying Investment Vehicles. We will also be subject to risks relating to the specific financial instruments that we, directly or indirectly, invest in, such as credit risk and liquidity risk.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Some of the financial instruments in which we, directly or indirectly, invest may not have a readily available market price. We will value these investments at fair value as determined in good faith pursuant to the valuation policy adopted for BXHF. There is no single standard for determining fair value in good faith. As a result, determining fair value requires that judgment be applied to the specific facts and circumstances of each financial instrument while employing a consistently applied valuation process. Because there is judgment in the valuation of illiquid investments, the fair value of investments reflected in the NAV may not necessarily reflect the prices that would actually be obtained when investments are realized, and such differences could be material.</span></div><div id="ie8493a2e77294448bf738d7b5cb3d914_575"></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Item 4.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Controls and Procedures</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Evaluation of Disclosure Controls and Procedures</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We maintain &#8220;disclosure controls and procedures,&#8221; as such term is defined in Rules 13a-15(e) and 15d-15(e) under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the &#8220;Exchange Act&#8221;), that are designed to ensure that information required to be disclosed by us in reports that we file or submit under the Exchange Act is recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time periods specified in the SEC rules and forms, and that such information is accumulated and communicated to our management, including our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, as appropriate, to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosure. In designing disclosure controls and procedures, our management necessarily was required to apply its judgment in evaluating the cost-benefit relationship of possible disclosure controls and procedures. The design of any disclosure controls and procedures also is based in part upon certain assumptions about the likelihood of future events, and there can be no assurance that any design will succeed in achieving its stated goals under all potential future conditions. Any controls and procedures, no matter how well designed and operated, can provide only reasonable assurance of achieving the desired objectives.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:9pt;text-indent:18pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Our management, including our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, evaluated the effectiveness of our disclosure controls and procedures pursuant to Rule 13a-15 under the Exchange Act as of the end of the period covered by this report. Based on that evaluation, our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer have concluded that, as of the end of the period covered by this report, our disclosure controls and procedures (as defined in Rule 13a-15(e) under the Exchange Act) are effective at the reasonable assurance level to accomplish their objectives of ensuring that information we are required to disclose in reports that we file or submit under the Exchange Act is recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time periods specified in the SEC rules and forms, and that such information is accumulated and communicated to our management, including our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, as appropriate, to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosure.</span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%"> </span></div><div style="height:36pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div
